newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil industry sales down 4.47 pct in March.
newsitem.headline: Brazil industry sales down 4.47 pct in March.

text.p: Brazilian industrial sales fell a seasonally adjusted 4.47 percent in March compared with February, an official with the private National Industry Confederation (CNI) said.
Sales in real terms, excluding seasonal factors, rose 10.42 percent, said Flavio Castello Branco, deputy head of the CNI's economic department.
Industry sales traditionally show strong growth in March after the holiday month of February.

March's increase in sales in real terms was lower than the 14-15 percent growth expected by the CNI, suggesting demand from consumers was being held back by personal debt levels, Castello Branco said.

"This is not a worrying figure," he said. "February's sales were also down and it seems we're in an adjustment phase. Families borrowed as much as they could to spend at the end of last year and now they're not able to buy much more on credit."
In February, seasonally adjusted sales were down 2.35 percent from January.
March industry sales were 6.71 percent higher than in the same month last year.
Castello Branco said he expected little month-on-month change in industry sales levels in April and May although small increases were possible.
"From an output point of view, there is no sign of an overheating of the economy although the situation looks very different in terms of the trade balance," he said.
Brazil posted a $3.989 billion trade deficit in the first four months of the year, leading the government to hike consumer sales taxes.
Referring to the March performance, he said industry functioned at a seasonally adjusted 77.4 percent of capacity, virtually unchanged from 77.5 percent in February.
He said the number of people employed in industry fell a seasonally adjusted 0.78 percent from February and was 3.89 percent lower than in March 1996.
The total number of hours worked in industry in March fell in seasonally adjusted terms, down 3.46 percent compared with February and down 4.77 percent from March 1996.
The total value of salaries paid rose 1.45 percent from February and was up 0.17 percent from March 1996, he said.
